# Backend API contract — `/api/v1`

**Verified against the real service.** This document was generated by reading
the FastAPI application on branch `claude/saas-link-discovery-backend-768jmc`
and by rendering its OpenAPI document (65 paths, 142 schemas). The frontend's
types are generated from that document, so this file is a human-readable index
rather than the source of truth — `frontend/src/types/api.generated.ts` is.

Regenerate after any backend schema change:

```bash
cd frontend
npm run codegen:api     # openapi-typescript → src/types/api.generated.ts
npm run typecheck       # every drift site becomes a compile error
```

## Envelopes

Every response is wrapped:

```jsonc
// single resource
{ "data": { … }, "meta": { … } }

// collection
{ "data": [ … ], "meta": { "page", "page_size", "total",
                           "total_pages", "has_next", "has_previous" } }

// failure — app/core/exceptions.py
{ "error": { "code": "PUBLISHER_NOT_FOUND", "message": "…", "details": { … } } }

// request-validation failure — FastAPI default
{ "detail": [ { "loc": ["body","name"], "msg": "…", "type": "…" } ] }
```

`src/lib/api/envelope.ts` unwraps the first two; `src/lib/api/errors.ts`
normalises both failure shapes into one `ApiError`.

## Authentication

Bearer tokens, **not** cookies. `POST /auth/login` returns a `TokenPair` in the
response body: a short-lived JWT access token plus a long-lived **opaque
refresh token**.

| Method | Path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/auth/register` | `{ email, password, first_name?, last_name?, tenant_name?, tenant_slug? }` → `TokenPair` |
| POST | `/auth/login` | `{ email, password, tenant_id? }` → `TokenPair` |
| POST | `/auth/refresh` | `{ refresh_token }` → `TokenPair` (refresh token is rotated) |
| POST | `/auth/logout` | `{ refresh_token?, all_sessions }` |
| POST | `/auth/select-tenant` | `{ tenant_id }` → `AccessTokenResponse`. Refresh token deliberately not rotated. |
| GET | `/auth/sessions` | Active sessions |
| DELETE | `/auth/sessions/{session_id}` | Revoke one |

Because the refresh token arrives in a JSON body, the frontend does **not** put
it in browser storage. Three Next.js route handlers
(`/api/session/{login,refresh,logout}`) proxy those three calls, keep the
refresh token in an HTTP-only `SameSite=Strict` cookie, and return only the
access token to the browser, which holds it in memory. See
`FRONTEND_ARCHITECTURE.md` §6.

`POST /me/password` takes `{ current_password, new_password, revoke_other_sessions }`.

## Tenant context

`X-Tenant-ID: <uuid>` on every workspace-scoped request. From
`app/api/dependencies/tenant.py`:

> The workspace can be named by the token's `tid` claim or by an `X-Tenant-ID`
> header. Both are treated identically: as a *request*, validated against
> `tenant_memberships` before anything else happens.

Membership is re-verified per request and PostgreSQL row-level security is
switched on for the validated tenant, so the header is context and never
authorization. Without either, the backend answers
`400 TENANT_CONTEXT_REQUIRED`.

## Identity, workspaces, RBAC

- `GET /me` → `{ user, tenants, active_tenant_id, permissions }`. Permissions
  are recomputed per request, so a revoked role takes effect immediately.
- `PATCH /me` (`first_name`, `last_name` only), `GET /me/tenants`
- `GET|POST /tenants`, `GET|PATCH /tenants/{id}`
- `GET|POST /tenants/{id}/members`, `PATCH|DELETE /tenants/{id}/members/{membership_id}`
- `GET /users`, `GET /users/{id}`
- `GET /permissions` — the permission catalogue that drives the role editor
- `GET|POST /roles`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE /roles/{id}`

Permission codes are `resource.action` (`app/rbac/catalog.py`, 51 codes).
Seeded role slugs: `owner`, `admin`, `seo_manager`, `seo_specialist`, `viewer`.
Roles are seeded **per tenant**, so a workspace can edit its own copies.

## Resources

| Resource | Endpoints |
| --- | --- |
| Client websites | `GET\|POST /client-websites`, `GET\|PATCH\|DELETE /client-websites/{id}` |
| Campaigns | `GET\|POST /campaigns`, `GET\|PATCH\|DELETE /campaigns/{id}`, `GET /campaigns/{id}/stats` |
| Publishers | `GET\|POST /publishers`, `GET\|PATCH\|DELETE /publishers/{id}`, `POST /publishers/{id}/qualify`, `POST /publishers/{id}/qualify-async` |
| Discovery | `POST /publishers/discover`, `GET /publishers/discovery-runs`, `GET /publishers/discovery-providers` |
| Opportunities | `GET\|POST /opportunities`, `GET\|PATCH\|DELETE /opportunities/{id}`, `POST /opportunities/{id}/{qualify,select,reject,transition}`, `GET /opportunities/state-machine` |
| AI content | `POST /opportunities/{id}/generate-content`, `GET /opportunities/{id}/content`, `POST /opportunities/{id}/content/{content_id}/review` |
| Submissions | `GET\|POST /submissions`, `GET\|PATCH\|DELETE /submissions/{id}`, `POST /submissions/{id}/{submit-for-review,approve,execute,verify,verify-async,transition}`, `GET /submissions/{state-machine,review-queue}` |
| Credentials | `GET\|POST /credentials`, `GET\|PATCH\|DELETE /credentials/{id}`, `POST /credentials/{id}/verify` |
| AI config | `GET\|PUT /ai/configs`, `DELETE /ai/configs/{id}`, `GET /ai/usage`, `GET /ai/usage/summary` |
| Audit | `GET /audit-logs` |
| Jobs | `GET /jobs`, `GET /jobs/{id}`, `GET /jobs/task-types` |

Collections accept `page`, `page_size`, `sort`, `order` plus resource-specific
filters (`q`, `status`, `campaign_id`, `min_quality_score`, `max_spam_score`,
`free_only`, …) — see the generated types for the exact set per endpoint.

### Enum values are SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE

`CampaignStatus`, `PublisherStatus`, `OpportunityStatus`, `SubmissionStatus`
and the rest serialise as `DRAFT`, `QUALIFIED`, `PENDING_APPROVAL` … The two
exceptions are `AiProvider` and `AiPurpose`, which are lowercase (`openai`,
`content_generation`). `frontend/src/config/enums.ts` mirrors every value with
a compile-time exhaustiveness check, so an added or renamed member fails
`npm run typecheck` rather than silently disappearing from a filter.

`DiscoveryRunRead.status` and `JobRead.status` are typed `str` rather than as
enum refs, so codegen cannot narrow them; their values are mirrored by hand in
`config/enums.ts` from `app/core/enums.py`.

### Asynchronous work

`POST /publishers/discover` with `run_async: true`, `qualify-async` and
`verify-async` return `JobAccepted { job_id, task_name, status, poll_url }`.
Discovery runs are observed through `GET /publishers/discovery-runs`, which the
UI polls at 3s while any run is `PENDING` or `RUNNING` and stops polling once
all are terminal. Nothing in the frontend blocks on a crawl.

### BYOK credentials

`CredentialCreate.secret` and `CredentialUpdate.secret` are write-only.
`CredentialRead` exposes `masked_key` and no secret field at all — so there is
no code path, present or future, by which the frontend could receive a
decrypted key. `DELETE /credentials/{id}` destroys the encrypted material
server-side.

### Free-listings scope

The backend has `PricingType` (`FREE|PAID|MIXED|UNKNOWN`) and raises
`PAID_PLACEMENT_NOT_ALLOWED`. The frontend pins `pricing_type=FREE` and
`free_only=true` on publisher listing and discovery requests, and every
`OpportunityType` value is a `FREE_*` listing, so paid inventory is never
fetched or offered (spec §73).

## Blocking backend defect (verified against a live instance)

Found by standing the backend up (Postgres 16, all 18 migrations, `scripts.seed`)
and driving it. **As committed on
`claude/saas-link-discovery-backend-768jmc`, no tenant-scoped endpoint can
succeed for any user**, so the frontend cannot be exercised against it.

**Symptom.** After a successful login, every workspace-scoped request answers
`403 TENANT_ACCESS_DENIED`, `GET /me` reports `tenants: []` and
`permissions: []`, and `GET /me/tenants` and `GET /tenants` return empty — even
though the membership row exists, is `ACTIVE` and `is_owner`.

**Root cause.** A chicken-and-egg deadlock between RLS and tenant resolution.
Migration `0017_rls_policies` enables RLS on `tenant_memberships`:

```sql
tenant_memberships_tenant_isolation  USING (tenant_id = app_current_tenant_id())
tenant_memberships_self_read         USING (user_id  = app_current_user_id())
```

`app/api/dependencies/tenant.py::get_tenant_context` then looks the membership
up *before* any context is established, on a session from
`get_unscoped_session` where both `app.current_tenant_id` and
`app.current_user_id` are NULL. Both policies evaluate false, the row is
invisible, `membership is None`, and the dependency raises `TenantAccessError`.
The same applies to `me.py`'s unscoped routes, which is why the workspace list
is empty.

Confirmed at the database level:

```
as buildseo_app, no context                      → 0 rows
as buildseo_app, SET app.current_user_id = …     → 1 row
```

**Affected call sites.** Every membership read that happens before a context
exists — at least three, found by fixing them one at a time:

1. `app/api/dependencies/tenant.py::get_tenant_context` — makes all
   tenant-scoped endpoints 403.
2. `app/api/v1/me.py::read_me` and `list_my_tenants` — make the workspace list
   empty, so nothing is selectable.
3. `app/auth/service.py::_require_membership` (used by `select_tenant` and by
   login's auto-select) — makes `POST /auth/select-tenant` 403, so a workspace
   cannot be chosen even when its id is known.

**Fix (backend).** `tenant_memberships_self_read` is clearly intended for
exactly this bootstrap case; nothing sets the user before the lookup.
`TenantAwareSession.set_tenant_context` already accepts `tenant_id=None`, so
binding the caller before the membership read is what is missing:

```python
await session.set_tenant_context(tenant_id=None, user_id=principal.user_id)
```

Because the same omission recurs at every such site, the durable fix is at the
session layer — bind the authenticated principal to the unscoped session once
(`get_unscoped_session`, given access to the principal) — rather than patching
each call site. Applying the per-site version locally did turn the 403s into
200s and made `/me` return both workspaces, so the diagnosis is verified rather
than inferred. **No backend change is committed here**; the local patches were
reverted and that branch is untouched.

**Consequence for the E2E suite.** `e2e/` runs against a real backend and does
not mock it. Until this is fixed the workflow specs cannot pass; `signIn`
raises a message naming this defect so the failure is not mistaken for a
frontend regression.

## Contract details this changed on the frontend

Two things the OpenAPI document does not convey, learned from the live service:

1. **`GET /me` derives `permissions` from the access token's `tid` claim, not
   from the `X-Tenant-ID` header** (`me.py::read_me` reads
   `principal.claimed_tenant_id`). A token from plain login carries no `tid`,
   so a client that only sets the header gets `permissions: []` and — with
   permission-gated navigation — an application with every feature hidden.
   `AuthProvider` therefore calls `POST /auth/select-tenant` during bootstrap
   to mint a workspace-scoped token, then re-reads `/me`.
2. **`POST /auth/login` ignores a `tenant_id` it cannot validate** and returns
   `active_tenant_id: null` rather than failing, so the client must not assume
   login yields a scoped session.

## Known gaps

Endpoints the frontend needs that the backend does not expose. **None of these
is mocked** — each is worked around using real endpoints, or the feature is
absent:

1. **No `/dashboard/*` endpoints.** There is no `summary`, `activity` or
   `campaign-progress` resource. `features/dashboard/api/use-dashboard.ts`
   composes the KPI figures from `meta.total` on the existing list endpoints
   (one `page_size: 1` request per figure), recent activity from
   `GET /audit-logs`, and progress from `GET /campaigns/{id}/stats`. If a
   summary endpoint is added, that hook is the only thing that changes.
2. **No `/audit-logs/{id}`.** The event drawer renders the row already held;
   `AuditLogRead.metadata` carries the structured context.
3. **No `/publishers/{id}/history`.** The publisher detail page builds its
   activity section from `GET /opportunities?publisher_id=…`.
4. **No `POST /roles/{id}/clone`.** Cloning is a create pre-filled with the
   source role's permission list, which the client already has.
5. **No user-preference endpoint.** Theme, sidebar state and default page size
   are per-device UI preferences stored in `localStorage`.
6. **No password-reset or email-verification endpoints**, and no email of any
   kind — matching the MVP scope (spec §11/§72). `lib/api/auth.ts` is shaped so
   they drop in without touching call sites.
7. **`GET /audit-logs` has no free-text search**, only `action`, `user_id`,
   `resource_type`, `resource_id` and a date range. The audit screen therefore
   filters by action rather than offering a search box that could not work.
